Write node:test integration tests for a meeting-room booking server in /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc. Load the Skill `tdd-workflow` if available (else skip). Node 22 built-ins only, no npm install. READ FIRST: /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/.team/notes/spec.md (the final spec, sections "Server" and "API"), /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/.team/notes/backend-api.md, and the shared helper /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/helpers/server.mjs (exports makeTempDir, removeDir, runToExit({env,cwd}) -> {code,signal,stdout,stderr}, startServer({env,cwd}) -> {port,output,stop(),exited} with PORT=0 default, request(port,{method,path,headers,body}) -> {status,headers,body,text,json()}, postBooking(port, obj|string|Buffer, headers?), rawRequest, useServer({before,after},{dataFileName,env}), VALID_BOOKING). Use these helpers; do not edit server.mjs or the helper (if you truly need a helper change, put a small local function in your test file). Code under test: /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs (read it only to understand; the SPEC is the authority). Create exactly two files: 1. /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/startup.test.mjs 2. /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/persistence.test.mjs Rules: `import { test, describe, before, after } from 'node:test'` and `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`. Exact equality for every value the spec names (assert.equal / deepEqual on full strings, never regex prefixes for spec'd text). Each file under 400 lines, functions under 50 lines; table-driven tests welcome. No console.log. Every spawned server must be stopped and every temp dir removed (use t.after / after hooks, try/finally). No test may depend on another test's order except inside one `describe` that shares a server. Never write anything into the project folder (use temp dirs as cwd). Tests must not hang. Run each file with `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc && node --test test/` until green. If a test fails because the SERVER violates the spec, do not weaken the test: keep it, and report the exact failure in your final message. startup.test.mjs must cover: - Invalid PORT values, each a separate test case: "abc", "65536", "+1", "-1", " 80", "80 ", "1e3", "0x10", "8080a", "99999999999999999999", "٣" (Arabic-Indic digit). Each: code 1, stdout exactly '', stderr is exactly one non-empty line ending in "\n" (assert /^[^\n]+\n$/ ) and contains no stack trace (no "\n at ", no "Error:" prefix lines beyond the one). Also: invalid PORT + DATA_FILE pointing at a directory → stderr is NOT 'cannot read data file ...' (PORT is checked first). - PORT "0" → stdout is exactly `listening on http://127.0.0.1:

\n` with p a number > 0 and != 0, and GET /api/rooms on p answers 200. After stopping (SIGKILL is used by stop), stdout still has only that one line and stderr is ''. - PORT with leading zeros: get a free port (net server listen(0), read port, close), start with PORT = "0" + String(port) → stdout exactly `listening on http://127.0.0.1:\n`. And PORT "65535" boundary: only check it is NOT rejected as invalid — if it exits, stderr must not be the same message as "65536" gives... simpler: skip 65535 unless free; if listen succeeds assert the stdout line with 65535. - Port in use: hold a port with a net server on 127.0.0.1; PORT=that → code 1, stdout '', one stderr line, no stack trace. Close the holder afterwards. - Default port 3000: try to bind 127.0.0.1:3000 with a net server. If the bind succeeds, keep holding it and run with PORT unset → code 1 (proves default is 3000); then also with PORT='' → code 1. Then release 3000 and start with PORT='' via spawn → stdout exactly `listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000\n` (stop it). If the initial bind fails with EADDRINUSE (something else uses 3000), run only the unset/'' → code 1 checks. Note startServer passes PORT '0' by default; to unset PORT pass env { PORT: undefined } (helper deletes undefined keys). - Data file read before listening: hold a port, run with that PORT and DATA_FILE = a file containing `{` → stderr exactly `cannot read data file \n` (data checked before bind). - DATA_FILE default and relative-to-cwd: cwd = temp dir holding `bookings.json` with fixture `{"nextId":3,"bookings":[{"id":2,"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}]}` and DATA_FILE unset → GET /api/bookings deepEqual {bookings:[that booking]}; same with DATA_FILE='' ; DATA_FILE='sub/x.json' relative with file at /sub/x.json. Then a POST with VALID_BOOKING-but-different-time against an unset DATA_FILE in an empty temp cwd creates /bookings.json (exists after POST) and the project root /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/bookings.json does NOT exist (check it did not exist before too; if it pre-exists skip that assertion). - ENOENT: missing file → starts, list empty `{"bookings":[]}`; missing folder 'nope/deeper/data.json' → starts, list empty, and the folder `nope` was not created after startup and after GETs. - Unreadable/invalid data → each case: code 1, stdout '', stderr EXACTLY `cannot read data file ${nameAsGiven}\n` where nameAsGiven is the DATA_FILE string as passed (relative or absolute, unresolved). Cases: DATA_FILE is a directory (absolute path); a relative directory name 'adir' (cwd temp); default name when `bookings.json` in cwd is a directory and DATA_FILE unset → `cannot read data file bookings.json\n`; same with DATA_FILE='' → `bookings.json`; non-ASCII name 'données.json' being a directory; empty file; whitespace-only file; '{'; 'null'; '[]'; '{}'; '"x"'; `{"nextId":1}`; `{"bookings":[]}`; `{"nextId":1,"bookings":{}}`; a booking with a missing key; a booking with an extra key; ENOTDIR (DATA_FILE='plain.txt/data.json' where plain.txt is a regular file). - No write at startup or for non-mutating requests: start with the valid fixture file; record its bytes and mtimeMs; send GET /api/rooms, GET /api/bookings, GET /api/bookings?date=2026-11-03, GET /, GET /app.js, GET /nope, HEAD /, OPTIONS /api/bookings, POST invalid (400 body), POST overlapping fixture (409), POST wrong content type (415), DELETE /api/bookings/999 (404), DELETE /api/bookings/abc (404); then file bytes and mtimeMs are unchanged. Same with a missing data file: after those requests the file still does not exist. - External changes not noticed: start with fixture, overwrite the file from the test with `{"nextId":1,"bookings":[]}`, GET /api/bookings still returns the fixture booking. persistence.test.mjs must cover: - Restart: in temp dir, start server; POST three bookings (different times, e.g. Aurora 2026-11-03 09:00-10:00, 10:00-11:00, 11:00-12:00) → ids exactly 1,2,3 and 201 bodies deepEqual {id, room, title, date, start, end} (exact keys). DELETE 3 and DELETE 1 → 204 each with empty body (body.length 0). Stop, start again with the same DATA_FILE → GET /api/bookings deepEqual [booking id 2] exactly; next POST gets id 4 (never reused, even the deleted last id 3). Restart a third time after deleting everything → next POST gets id 5. - Save failure: DATA_FILE = /missing/data.json (folder absent) → POST valid → status 500, body deepEqual {error:'internal error'}, content-type exactly 'application/json; charset=utf-8'; GET list → {bookings:[]}; the server still running (GET /api/rooms 200). Then mkdir /missing → POST the SAME booking → 201 with id exactly 1 (next id unchanged and no phantom booking causing 409). Then remove the folder (rm -r) → DELETE /api/bookings/1 → 500 {error:'internal error'}; GET list still holds booking 1; POST a second booking → 500; recreate folder → POST a non-overlapping booking → id exactly 2; DELETE 1 → 204. Then restart → list is [booking 2] and next id is 3. - Concurrency: 10 identical overlapping POSTs sent at once (Promise.all) → exactly one 201, nine 409 each with body exactly {error:'room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00'}; list has exactly one booking. Then 10 concurrent non-overlapping POSTs (different rooms/hours) → all 201, ids are 10 distinct consecutive integers; after restart all 11 bookings are present and the next POST gets the next id after the max. Also concurrent mix: POST overlapping + DELETE of the existing booking at once → results consistent with some sequential order (either 409 then 204, or 204 then 201) and the final list matches that order. - Delete persistence: data file content after each change is valid JSON (parse it) — do not assert its layout beyond parsing. Final message: list the files, the number of tests, pass/fail, and any spec violation you found (exact request, expected, actual). Keep it short.

content.content: 1 # Spec — meeting-room booking app (owner: supervisor, verbatim user requirements; FINAL, do not ask questions) 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Tests use node:test. Do not use the Fable model. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 ## Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet.
